## TL;DR

R 4.5.0 was releases on 2025-04-11 and is now available on Wynton
through the [CBI] software stack. I have validated that almost all
CRAN and Bioconductor packages can be installed with this new version.


## Using R

To use R 4.5.0, which is the new default version, load it as:

```r
{alice@dev3 ~}$ module load CBI r
```

Then you can run R interactively from the terminal using:

```r
{alice@dev3 ~}$ R --quiet

> getRversion()
[1] '4.5.0'
```

To use R 4.5.0 in RStudio, just follow our [RStudio documentation].


## Re-installing R packages

As usual when we move to a new version (e.g. from R 4.4 to R 4.5), any
R packages installed in the previous version (R 4.4) are _not_
available in the new version (R 4.5). This is not the case when we
move from one patch version to another, e.g. R 4.5.0 to R 4.5.1. With
the release of R 4.5.0 we have to start from scratch and reinstall any
packages we need. So, don't be surprised when `library(dplyr)` gives
an error on "there is no package called 'dplyr'". Also, when
installing your first package in a new version of R, R will ask you:

```r
> install.packages("dplyr")
Warning in install.packages("dplyr") :
  'lib = "/wynton/home/cbi/shared/software/_rocky8/R-4.5.0-gcc13/lib64/R/library"'
  is not writable
Would you like to use a personal library instead? (yes/No/cancel)
```

Answer **yes** to this and anything else that R asks you to
confirm. Doing so will make sure you get a smooth ride when using R.
This is all explained in our [R documentation].


## You must deactivate Conda to use this R installation

Conda does not play well with other software tools installed on the
system, especially not with programming tools such as Python and
R. From experience working with Wynton users, Conda causes more
problems for users than any of other software tool on Wynton.  When it
comes to R, having Conda activated when installing a R package causes
that R package to depend on your personal Conda setup. If your Conda
setup gets updated later on, which it will, there is a great risk some
of your R packages breaks. You will get hard-to-troubleshoot, obscure
"library" errors when you try to load those R packages. It is a very
tedious task trying to figure out which R package are affected, so
they can be re-installed.

In the past, `module load CBI r` would _warn_ about these problems, if
it detected that Conda is activated. However, some users did not
understand the importance of that warning, and some users are unaware
that they have Conda activated. Ignoring the warning had no immediate
impact, which could lead to thinking that "R seems to work fine with
Conda." Starting with R 4.5.0, `module load CBI r` will now give an
_error_ and refuse to load if Conda is activated, e.g.

```sh
(base) {alice@dev3 ~}$ module load CBI r
Lmod has detected the following error: Using the 'r' module when a Conda
environment is active risks resulting in hard-to-troubleshoot errors due
to library conflicts. Make sure to deactivate the currently active Conda
'base' environment before loading this module, e.g. 'conda deactivate'.

(base) {alice@dev3 ~}$ R --version
-bash: R: command not found
```

If you experience this, follow the instructions in the error message
and deactivate Conda first, then retry:

```sh
(base) {alice@dev3 ~}$ conda deactivate
{alice@dev3 ~}$ module load CBI r

{alice@dev3 ~}$ R --version
R version 4.5.0 (2025-04-11) -- "How About a Twenty-Six"
Copyright (C) 2025 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu
...
```


## Validation

Just as with previous versions of R available via the [CBI] stack, I
have validated that nearly all R packages on [CRAN] and [Bioconductor]
can be installed out of the box using this new R 4.5.0 installation.

Specifically, I have confirmed that 22,582 (99.1%) out of
22,371[^cran-count] CRAN packages and 2,??? out of 2,308[^bioc-count]
Bioconductor 3.21 packages are straightforward to install. A small
number of packages require some extra love - see our [R documentation]
for guidance on installing those.

The 47 CRAN and ?? Bioconductor packages that failed to install do so
either because they depend on a system library that is not available
on the cluster, or because they have bugs preventing them from being
installed out of the box.


[CRAN]: https://cran.r-project.org
[Bioconductor]: https://www.bioconductor.org
[CBI]: https://wynton.ucsf.edu/hpc/software/software-repositories.html#repository_cbi
[R documentation]: https://wynton.ucsf.edu/hpc/howto/r.html
[RStudio documentation]: https://wynton.ucsf.edu/hpc/howto/rstudio.html

[^cran-count]: CRAN: `nrow(available.packages(repos = "https://cran.r-project.org"))`
[^bioc-count]: Bioconductor: `nrow(available.packages(repos = "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.21/bioc"))`
